question: What lock-on values does saved game data store for gadget launchers, the laser designator and vehicle missiles, and do the named registry rows agree with the assets' own locking controller objects?

sourceFacts.method: Class_9a3efaa2 was identified from LockingController_Flare; every object of that class in the saved gadget and vehicle files was listed (106 objects, 62 files). Six fields were named by equality with the six registry rows of the same controller (LockTime, UnLockTime, ReleaseTime, ReleaseOnNewTargetTime, MinimumRange, RayLength): all six agree for F16, JAS39, AH64E air-to-ground, Bradley, CV90 and both PLD controllers.

control.description: Six named fields of the first WB_Javelin and first VB_VEH_Airplane_F22 locking controller objects.

inference: Field names are assigned by value equality with registry rows, not by a type descriptor.

For air-to-air controllers the registry expresses the painted case as a longer ray length (650 to 780, 665 to 800) with equal lock time, while most blueprints hold two objects with ray length 800 and lock times 1 and 0.625. EA's 1.3.1.0 note of a 20% lock-range bonus for painted targets corresponds to the registry form (780 / 650 = 1.2); this is a correspondence, not a control.
unresolved: Which object of a pair applies to painted targets, and whether a match uses the registry rows or the own objects.
Units of ray length and of the times.
Which gadget the registry owners PrimaryLockingController (lock time 1.5, ray length 687.5) and SecondaryLockingController (1.4, 550) belong to; no own object carries those values.
Names of the other 32 fields of the class.
siteImpact: None. No Analyzer data, simulation or UI change.

leads.title: Lock-on values for gadget launchers, the laser designator and vehicle missiles
leads.summary: 106 locking controller objects in 62 gadget and vehicle files store lock time, unlock and release times, minimum range and ray length; 636 raw-offset checks matched. Registry rows agree with own objects except the ray length of air-to-air default controllers.
leads.reopenWhen: An in-game lock-time or lock-range measurement on painted and unpainted targets, a type descriptor naming the fields, or a game update that changes a controller.
leads.statusNote: Source values only; field names by value equality; units and runtime use unconfirmed.
